tagline: Out across the plains and back down through the mountains.
intro: The byway follows old trade routes, rail beds and footpaths. From Mountainair it runs north across the plains through Estancia to Moriarty, west to Tijeras, then south on NM 337 through Chilili and back down through Manzano. The eastern and southern branches keep to the plains, the western one to the mountains.
South of Tijeras the road passes the forested canyons of the Cibola National Forest, Tunnel Canyon and Otero Canyon among them, with Cedro Campground and the Pine Flat picnic ground.

moments.title: Estancia
moments.text: The county seat turns up on a map of 1779, drawn by Don Bernardo de Miera y Pacheco, marked as a town destroyed by enemies.

moments.title: Tijeras
moments.text: Tijeras sits in the canyon that served as the corridor between the plains and the Rio Grande settlements, beside a pueblo that had some 200 rooms at first and was lived in from about 1313 to 1425.

moments.title: Manzano
moments.text: Twenty-six people live in Manzano, named for the apple tree, and the center of population of New Mexico falls right here, with the Quarai mission ruins nearby.
